blocks.content: The crust is the outermost, ultra-thin solid skin of the Earth, divided into light continental sial and dense oceanic sima.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The crust is the outermost solid shell of Earth, comprising less than 1% of the planet's total volume.
Continental crust is predominantly composed of granitic rocks rich in silica and aluminium, collectively termed SIAL.
Oceanic crust is thinner, denser, and made up primarily of basaltic rocks rich in silica and magnesium, known as SIMA.
Oxygen is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust by weight (46.6%), followed by silicon (27.7%) and aluminium (8.1%).
The boundary marking the transition between the Earth's crust and the upper mantle is called the Mohorovičić discontinuity.
Oxygen is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust, whereas Iron is the most abundant element in the Earth as a whole.
The Mohorovičić discontinuity (Moho boundary) separates the crust from the mantle and is frequently asked in UPSC/SSC exams.
Continental crust (SIAL) is less dense (2.7 g/cm³) than oceanic crust (SIMA, 3.0 g/cm³), which causes continents to float higher on the mantle.
